abstract: Machine learning models are increasingly used to not only inform, but make decisions. Sometimes platforms add value by pooling data across contexts to improve models' decision making---but when the optimal decision differs by context, pooling may not increase accuracy. We argue that a platform storing starkly distinct models across contexts nevertheless captures a model comparison externality. Together, these models reflect how decision makers respond differently to the same data in the current equilibrium. Policymakers can use this differentiation to prioritize interventions; firms can learn how they are already differentiated from competitors to focus future investments. Our evidence comes from an AI hiring platform used by large employers of low-skill workers. The platform uses a standardized psychometric assessment to create firm-specific models estimating each application's retention likelihood at that firm. Each firm's model is highly predictive for itself but no better than chance at other firms. We use these models to create a firm-application matrix: each firm scores each application, not only the ones it receives. An application's improved retention likelihood if submitted to a different firm is highly heterogeneous based on traits. Further, these gains are due to two distinct mechanisms. Finally, firms value traits differently even in this low skill market: they disagree about whether important traits improve or worsen retention at the margin. These insights are only possible when a platform can access both the full application pool and each firm-specific model. We explain the value of these insights to firms, policymakers, and platforms.

ob.ai_reason: 核心研究机器学习招聘决策及平台市场
ob.tldr: 利用低技能岗位AI招聘平台的企业留任模型，考察跨情境汇总数据能否改善决策及平台如何传递市场信息。企业模型仅对自身申请有效，跨企业预测近乎随机；交叉评分显示，换岗带来的留任收益高度异质，且企业对边际特征的价值判断明显分歧，表明差异化模型可揭示竞争定位与干预对象。

title: Learning about Markets from Models: Evidence from an AI Hiring Platform
title_zh: 通过模型了解市场：来自 AI 招聘平台的证据
